code: const unsigned char *uc = CAST(const unsigned char *, b->fbuf);
note: magic_buffer input bytes are exposed to the JSON detector as the start pointer uc.
The input length sets the exclusive end pointer ue for subsequent JSON parsing.
The detector passes the input cursor and end pointer into the recursive parser.
For this candidate the first input byte '[' is consumed and dispatches to array parsing with uc now pointing at the following space.
The cursor positioned after '[' is passed to json_parse_array while ue remains the end of the two-byte input.
json_skip_space consumes the trailing space and can make uc equal to ue, but the code does not enforce the required uc < ue before the next dereference.
With uc equal to ue, dereferencing *uc reads one byte past the two-byte input buffer.
